# Evidence for this task

## Endpoint, merge, and strata

The adverse-event table has 2,694 records. Severity is reduced to one observation per subject as the maximum `AESEV` over all that subject's adverse-event records, with no event-term filter. Thus the endpoint is maximum severity across all recorded adverse events, not a COVID-specific endpoint.

The reduction gives 1,000 subjects and is merged with a 1,000-subject demographics/exposure table. There are 209 missing severity values and 143 missing `AEHS` values in the source fields; restricting to complete analysis variables leaves 791 subjects.

The `patients_seen` strata and complete-case counts are:

| Stratum | Merged subjects | Excluded for missing analysis values | Complete cases |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 1–50 | 835 | 177 | 658 |
| 51–100 | 129 | 21 | 108 |
| >100 | 36 | 11 | 25 |

## Separate ordinary Pearson tests

Each table is tested separately with an ordinary Pearson chi-square test:

| `patients_seen` stratum | \(X^2\) | df | Nominal p-value | Minimum expected count | Cells with expected <5 | Cells with expected <1 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1–50 | 9.420743463606744 | 3 | 0.024189637931453605 | 5.7097 | 0/8 | 0/8 |
| 51–100 | 3.4529649916646816 | 3 | 0.32691383506649596 | 1.8889 | 4/8 | 0/8 |
| >100 | 2.6785714285714284 | 3 | 0.4438811470106675 | 0.3200 | 6/8 | 4/8 |

## Interpretation limits

Three separate tests were run without a multiplicity correction. If a Bonferroni sensitivity check is reported, compare three times the smallest nominal probability with 0.05. The 51–100 and especially the >100 table also have sparse expected cells, making the usual chi-square approximation weak. These issues, together with the all-adverse-event maximum-severity endpoint, should accompany any interpretation.

# Patient-volume modification of adverse-event severity after BCG vaccination

Petra van Dijk, Omar Rahal, Mei-Ling Chou, and Benjamin K. Foster

## Abstract

Occupational patient volume may modify the distribution of adverse-event severity among vaccinated healthcare workers. We reduced all adverse-event records to each participant’s maximum severity, merged treatment assignment and patient-volume strata, and performed separate Pearson tests within 1–50, 51–100, and >100 patients-seen categories. Only the >100 stratum crossed the nominal 0.05 threshold, whereas the two lower-volume strata showed no treatment-associated distributional difference. The highest-volume group contained sparse severe-event cells, limiting the chi-square approximation, and the three stratum tests were not multiplicity corrected. These results provide exploratory evidence of a treatment–severity association among the most heavily exposed workers.

Current request:
Define the subject-level adverse-event severity endpoint and clarify which events contribute to it.
Merge with the patients_seen exposure field, retain complete cases, and form its three patient-volume strata.
Construct the maximum-severity-by-treatment observed table within each stratum.
Calculate the expected counts and assess cell sparsity in each table.
Compute the three ordinary Pearson chi-square statistics and upper-tail p-values.
Which strata meet nominal 0.05, and how do multiplicity, sparse cells, and endpoint scope limit interpretation?
